correctness.rationale: The index-two checkerboard annihilator pairs exactly two Fourier aliases, with midpoint u in the full cube [-pi/2,pi/2]^d and sign vector epsilon. The actual RESULT.md derives the 2×2 unitary fiber with entries (1,1) and c+i gamma(v·u ± pi v·epsilon/2), divided by sqrt2. Its Gram trace and determinant yield roots lambda±; maximum midpoint |c+i gamma m|² equals Q=(Re c)²+(|Im c|+gamma pi ||v||1/2)². The lower spectral root increases with squared alias gap z², the upper root does too, so essential sharp bounds are lambda_-(s), lambda_+(L), s=min_epsilon|v·epsilon|, L=||v||1. For s=0 a positive-measure alias cell has a rank-one fiber, hence genuinely infinite-dimensional nullspace; otherwise bounded below. Rademacher identity averages (v·epsilon)² to 1, yielding s≤1, L≥1 with equality in L only for signed coordinate directions. Scalar Q uniquely minimized at c=0. Optimizing q=gamma² pi² gives q=2, sharp A=1−1/sqrt2 and B=1+1/sqrt2, condition 1+sqrt2, with strict uniqueness; Taylor root expansion at s↓0 gives quadratic law. Continuous proof not reduced to random fibers.
